question: Can you walk me through the architecture of the real‑time multi‑camera semantic segmentation system you built for the Kerala MVD, specifically how you designed the pipeline to achieve low latency and handle synchronization across multiple video streams?
answer: I built a real-time multi-camera semantic segmentation system for the Kerala MVD,where the main challenges were low latency inference and synchronization acrossmultiple IP camera streams.Architecture Overview:- Multiple IP cameras (front, side-front, side-back)- Independent video ingestion per camera- Central inference and rule-evaluation pipelineSynchronization Strategy:- No hard frame-level synchronization- Each stream runs independently- Frames are timestamped with camera_id and frame_id- Soft synchronization using a 100 to 150 ms time window- Violations are evaluated over multiple framesLow-Latency Design:- Lightweight segmentation models (YOLO-Seg, DDRNet, UNet variants)- Optimized input resolution- GPU warm-up at startup- Asynchronous pipeline using queues- Capture, inference, and post-processing are decoupledRule Evaluation:- Temporal consistency instead of single-frame decisions- Violations confirmed over N consecutive frames- Evidence aggregated across cameras- Reduces false positives from shadows and noiseReliability:- Asynchronous recording per camera- Violation clips stored separately- System remains operational even if one stream dropsKey Design Decision:- Synchronization at the logic layer instead of frame level- This ensured low latency, fault tolerance, and scalability
